- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward 70–75 range after a spike, model often holds too high; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.  
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 1.00 repeated), model tends to lag; forecast should be slightly ahead of true price by 1–2 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply downward correction of 3–5% for next 30d.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model often misjudges volatility; use 1–2% smoothing filter to dampen extreme swings.
